methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: CLIL Synthesis (The Review Station)
content: Problem: Students learn Science and Math vocabulary in isolated weeks. They may struggle to categorize and recall these specialized terms across different domains.

SCIENTISTS have DISCOVERED that the WATER CYCLE IS DRIVEN by the SUN, which is the LARGEST and HOTTEST object in our SOLAR SYSTEM.

Today, we are reviewing cycles and math words!

Max loves math. "In math, addition (phép cộng) makes numbers bigger. We use the word 'plus'. Subtraction (phép trừ) makes numbers smaller. We use the word 'minus'."
Cycles and math operations both follow special rules. Science and math are connected!

listening_script.text: Detective Max is reviewing his science files today. "We learned about living and non-living things," says Max. "A cat is living because it breathes and grows. A stone is non-living." "We also learned about animals," says Luna. "A dog is a vertebrate because it has a backbone. It is a mammal." "Birds are oviparous because they lay eggs!" says Pip. Animals live in different places. This is called a habitat. Camels live in the hot desert. Polar bears live in the cold polar regions. Science helps us understand the amazing natural world!
dictation: A cat is a living thing.

listening_script.text: Today, we are reviewing cycles and math words! "The life cycle of a frog is amazing," says Pip. "First, it is an egg. Next, it is a tadpole. Finally, it is an adult frog." "The water cycle is also a process," says Luna. "The sun heats the water. The water evaporates." Max loves math. "In math, addition makes numbers bigger. We use the word 'plus'. Subtraction makes numbers smaller. We use the word 'minus'." Cycles and math operations both follow special rules. Science and math are connected!
